land.text: Arpad's lands, 'converted into two provinces' in 740 BC; 'Afterward Arpad served a provincial capital'

successors.note: The Bit Agusi page's last stage (743-740 BC) is 'reduced to the status of an Assyrian province'; the neo-hittite-states dossier (me-04-a) also records Arpad's capture in 740. The Bit Agusi page says Arpad's revolt of 720 is not on it.

capitals.name: Arpad (Tell Rifaat)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Bit Agusi; its Neo-Hittite states shape of -900 holds Arpad's lands inside a larger Syro-Anatolian block. The page gives no area, only 'from A'zaz in the north to Hamath in the south' at its maximum and Nampigi, Arpad and 'later Aleppo'; a 50 km circle round Tell Rifaat (about 7,000 km2) is the researcher's reading of the early core.

correction.text: Bit Agusi (the Kingdom of Arpad) 'from A'zaz in the north to Hamath in the south', including Nampigi, Arpad and later Aleppo; the Idlib governorate to the south is Hamath's (Luhuti, from c. 796 BC)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: stage 6 (754-744 BC), 'Bit Agusi, now known as the Kingdom of Arpad, rises to prominence'; the Aleppo region (about 18,000 km2), which holds the early core. The page dates 'later' Aleppo to no year, so 754 is a bridge; the southern edge toward Hamath is not drawn because Luhuti (Idlib) belongs to Hamath in the hamath dossier.

wars.name: Shalmaneser III's subjugation of Bit Agusi
wars.outcome: Arame submits in 858 BC; Bit Agusi is subjugated to Assyria in stage 2 (841-823 BC) and frees itself c. 823 BC.
wars.note: The page names no battles or campaigns of Shalmaneser III; the Battle of Qarqar page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Qarqar) does not list Bit Agusi among the coalition.

wars.name: The coalition against Zakkur of Hamath
wars.outcome: 'Zakkur survived the siege' at Tell Afis; 'led by the king of Bit Agusi' and incited by Ben-Hadad III. Adad-nirari III later had Shamshi-ilu mediate a border dispute between Zakkur and Atarshumki I of Arpad.
wars.note: The Bit Agusi page is silent on the coalition ('Coalition against Zakkur of Hamath (c. 796): page silent'); the Zakkur page supplies it, undated except Zakkur's c. 785 BC.

certainty.note: The page gives only the maximum extent (A'zaz to Hamath); the Hamath border was a dispute settled by Assyria c. 785.

notes: Cliopatria has no Bit Agusi; its Neo-Hittite states row (-1180..-717) holds the same land and the neo-hittite-states dossier (me-04-a) already has the 740 loss of 'Arpad (Bit Agusi) and its lands' with the same year, so the renderer should not count the 740 loss twice. me-04-a suggested the slug 'arpad'; the Wikipedia title gives bit-agusi. The stages on the page are not years: stage 1 (858-ca. 842), 2 (841-823), 3 (c. 823), 4 (until ca. 805), 5 (ca. 800-754), 6 (754-744), 7 (743-740). The Aram-Damascus supremacy over Bit Agusi (stage 4) and Aleppo's addition (stage 6) are low-confidence readings. Not drawn: the Sefire treaty vassalage to Bar-Ga'yah of KTK (undated, within 754-744) and Arpad's revolt of 720 (page silent). Page budget: three pages.
